svg.title: OSPF with BGP/MPLS VPN backbone

cc:Work.dc:title: OSPF with BGP/MPLS VPN backbone
cc:Work.dc:description: Diagram of using OSPF as the routing protocol between a service provider's BGP/MPLS VPN backbone and a customer. The service provider's equipment is labeled as PE (provider edge) and the customer's equipment is labeled as CE (customer edge). The boxes represent different sites within the customer's network. Area 0 is multi-homed with two PEs. Area 1 is single-homed, and the PE acts as an area border router (ABR) between area 1 and area 0. Area 2 comprises two different sites, each with its own PE ABR, but also an internal backdoor link which is the preferred link rather than the service provider's network. Area 3 is similar two area 2, but is also a configured with a sham link by the service provider. In this case, the sham link is the preferred link between the two sites.
